summary: IDS feed s172_triple is degraded: 3.09 Gbps microbursts overload 1 Gbps IDS port (309%), 80% traffic encrypted exceeds 60% tolerance, and 8.6% duplicates waste inspection capacity.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peak at 3.09 Gbps vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (309% in 5 intervals). Average rate hides 1ms bursts that overflow the tool NIC/buffers, so broker shows no drops but tool drops traffic locally.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops packets at ingress during bursts, creating blind spots and breaking stateful detection/stream reassembly; attacks in bursts are missed.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across multiple IDS members or a higher-capacity cluster to keep per-tool rate <80% of 1 Gbps and preserve full payload inspection this IDS requires.

findings.root_cause: 80% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) vs IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is opaque without decryption - likely TLS 1.3 everywhere with no broker-side SSL visibility configured.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS can only do metadata/heuristics on 80% of traffic; payload signatures, exploit and C2 detection are blind, sharply reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS at packet broker/visibility tier and feed cleartext to IDS (with privacy bypass for sensitive categories) to restore payload inspection while respecting IDS full-payload requirement.

findings.root_cause: 8.6% duplicates (282/3282 packets) indicates overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or aggregation of both sides of a TAP without deduplication in the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU doing duplicate signature matching and state tracking, inflates alerts/events, and reduces headroom already constrained by overload.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to drop identical packets arriving within milliseconds before delivery, freeing IDS capacity for unique traffic.
